equation_request.abstract: We systematically investigated perfect state transfer between antipodal nodes of discrete time quantum walks on variants of the cycles C4, C6 and C8 for three choices of coin operator. Perfect state transfer was found, in general, to be very rare, only being preserved for a very small number of ways of modifying the cycles. We observed that some of our useful modifications of C4 could be generalised to an arbitrary number of nodes, and present three families of graphs which admit quantum walks with interesting dynamics either in the continuous time walk, or in the discrete time walk for appropriate selections of coin and initial conditions. These dynamics are either periodicity, perfect state transfer, or very high fidelity state transfer. These families are modifications of families known not to exhibit periodicity or perfect state transfer in general. The robustness of the dynamics is tested by varying the initial state, interpolating between structures and by adding decoherence.

specification.problem: Discrete-time coined quantum walk on the cycle C_N (N=4 as the smallest instance, optionally N=6 or 8) with coin in {Hadamard, Grover, DFT}. Test perfect state transfer (PST) from node 0 to the antipodal node N/2 by computing the antipodal probability P(t) over t=1..T. Modified graphs, decoherence and the continuous-time comparison are out of scope.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest instance: C4 with a 2-qubit position register and a 1-qubit coin, with the Hadamard coin and the moving-shift convention. Read out P(t) from the statevector for t=1..T with T small (e.g. 8). Out of scope: the specific modified graphs, the Grover/DFT coins on degree>2 graphs, the enumeration of modifications, the interpolation ancilla, decoherence, the continuous-time walk, and the three families of graphs. The abstract does not specify these.

symbols.meaning: conditional shift on position and coin
symbols.domain: permutation unitary on C^N tensor C^2

symbols.meaning: initial state, node 0 with coin state |c_0\rangle
probability of being at antipodal node N/2 at step t, summed over coin states

equations.label: Shift operator
equations.description: Coin 0 increments position, coin 1 decrements it, mod N. This is the moving shift on the plain cycle, implemented with an incrementer/decrementer ladder.
equations.justification: The sketch proposes this convention. The abstract does not give the shift. The sketch states a flip-flop assumption, but this is the simple moving shift for the degree-2 cycle, so the convention is unresolved.
assumptions: Moving shift used for the cycle
Flip-flop convention for higher-degree graphs not specified

equations.label: Walk step
equations.description: One step applies the coin to the coin qubit and then the shift. The state at step t is U^t applied to the initial state.
equations.justification: Standard coined discrete-time quantum walk definition.

equations.label: Initial state
equations.description: Walker at node 0 with a coin state set by Bloch angles. It is prepared with Ry(theta) and Rz(phi) or X/H/S gates.
equations.justification: The abstract mentions varying the initial state. The specific parametrization comes from the sketch.

equations.label: Antipodal transfer probability
equations.description: Probability at the antipodal node, summed over coin states. PST occurs at t if P(t)=1 within 1e-9. Otherwise it is high fidelity if P(t) is close to 1.
equations.abstract_quote: perfect state transfer between antipodal nodes of discrete time quantum walks
equations.justification: The abstract defines PST between antipodal nodes. The sum over coin states follows the sketch's assumption.
assumptions: The coin state at arrival is ignored

equations.label: Periodicity test
equations.description: The walk is periodic at t when the return amplitude has unit modulus.
equations.abstract_quote: either periodicity, perfect state transfer, or very high fidelity state transfer
equations.justification: The abstract names periodicity as one of the dynamics. The test is the standard definition.

registers.name: pos
registers.role: node index, little-endian integer encoding, qubit 0 is the least significant bit

specification.initial_state: Node 0 with a chosen coin state (default |0>), prepared with X/H/S gates or Ry/Rz.

steps.description: Prepare the initial state on pos=0 and the coin.
Apply the coin gate to the coin qubit.
Apply the conditional shift S, with increment when coin=0 and decrement when coin=1, using CX and multi-controlled X gates.
Repeat for t=1..T, with a separate circuit per t and no measurements. Read the statevector and compute P(t) and the return amplitude.

specification.measurement: None for statevector reading. If counts are needed, measure only the position qubits. With little-endian bits, the last character of the key is pos bit 0.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute P(t) for each t from the statevector. Declare PST if max_t P(t) >= 1-1e-9, and compute |<psi0|U^t|psi0>| for periodicity.
assumptions: Smallest instance is C4 with the Hadamard coin
Coin and shift conventions are as in eq_1
Antipodal node is N/2, starting at node 0

The three coins are Hadamard, Grover and DFT. Grover and DFT coins are not applicable to a 1-qubit coin on the plain cycle, since Grover on 2 dimensions equals a Pauli-like reflection and DFT on 2 dimensions equals H.
Qubit count: 3 for C4 and 4 for C8, within the cap
